Assertion (A): (1 + tan²θ) cos²θ = 1 for every acute angle θ.
Reason (R): 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

Assertion (A): There is an acute angle θ for which sec θ = 3/5.
Reason (R): In a right-angled triangle the hypotenuse is the longest side, so sec θ = hypotenuse/base is always greater than 1 for an acute angle θ.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

text: Evaluate: 4 sin²30° + 3 tan²60° − 2 sec²45°.
If sin (A + B) = 1 and cos (A − B) = √3/2, where 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, find the values of A and B.
If sin θ + cos θ = 5/4, find the value of sin θ cos θ and hence of tan θ + cot θ.
Find the value of p if p sin 30° + 4 cos²60° = 3 tan²45° + cosec 30°.
If 13 sin A = 5 and A is acute, evaluate (5 sin A − 2 cos A)/tan A.
Prove that cos θ/(1 + sin θ) + (1 + sin θ)/cos θ = 2 sec θ.
Prove that sin θ (1 + tan θ) + cos θ (1 + cot θ) = sec θ + cosec θ.
A vertical tower casts a shadow 15 m long on level ground when the angle of elevation of the Sun is 60°. Find the height of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)

From a point on level ground 30 m from the foot of a vertical pole, the angle of elevation of the top of the pole is 30°. Find the height of the pole and the distance of the top of the pole from the point. (Leave answers in surd form.)

A boy 1.5 m tall stands 20 m away from a vertical pole. The angle of elevation of the top of the pole from his eyes (take eye level as 1.5 m above ground) is 45°. Find the height of the pole above the ground.
Prove that (cot θ − cos θ)/(cot θ + cos θ) = (cosec θ − 1)/(cosec θ + 1).
Prove that (sec θ − cos θ)/(sec θ + cos θ) = sin²θ/(1 + cos²θ).
Prove that (1 + sin θ)/(1 − sin θ) = (sec θ + tan θ)².
Prove that tan²θ/(1 + tan²θ) + cot²θ/(1 + cot²θ) = 1.
Prove that (cosec θ − sin θ)(sec θ − cos θ)(tan θ + cot θ) = 1.
If tan θ + sin θ = m and tan θ − sin θ = n, prove that m² − n² = 4√(mn).

A flagstaff 10 m high stands on top of a tower. From a point on level ground, the angles of elevation of the bottom and the top of the flagstaff are 30° and 45° respectively. Find the height of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)

Two points A and B lie on level ground on opposite sides of a 30 m high tower and in line with its foot. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower from A and B are 30° and 60° respectively. Find the distance AB. (Use √3 = 1.73)
Evaluate: (sin 35°/cos 55°)² + tan 20° tan 70° + 3 sec 25° sin 65° − 2 tan 17° tan 73°.
If 15 cot A = 8 and A is acute, find sin A, sec A and the value of (1 + sin A)/(1 − sin A).

A tower stands on top of a 20 m high building. From a point P on level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the building is 45° and that of the top of the tower is 60°. Find (i) the distance of P from the foot of the building and (ii) the height of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)

A boat approaches the foot of a 90 m high lighthouse in a straight line. A keeper at the top first sees the boat at an angle of depression of 30°; 6 minutes later the angle of depression is 60°. Assuming the boat moves at constant speed, find (i) the distance the boat covered in the 6 minutes, (ii) its speed in metres per minute, and (iii) how much more time it will take to reach the foot of the lighthouse. (Use √3 = 1.73)

A point is 40 m above the surface of a lake. The angle of elevation of a cloud from this point is 45° and the angle of depression of the cloud's reflection in the lake, from the same point, is 60°. Find the height of the cloud above the lake. (Use √3 = 1.73)

Standing on the roof of a 24 m high building, a surveyor observes the foot of a transmission tower at an angle of depression of 45° and its top at an angle of elevation of 30°. The tower and building are on level ground. Find (i) the horizontal distance between the building and the tower, and (ii) the height of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)

An aeroplane flies horizontally at a constant height of 900 m directly away from an observer on the ground. When first seen, its angle of elevation is 45°; after 20 seconds it is 30°. Find the distance flown in 20 seconds and the speed of the aeroplane in m/s and in km/h. (Use √3 = 1.73)

The angle of elevation of the top of a vertical tower from a point A on level ground is 60°. From a point B on a vertical pole, 20 m above A, in the same vertical plane as the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 45°. Find (i) the height of the tower and (ii) the horizontal distance of the tower from the pole. (Use √3 = 1.73)

Kite flying. Aarav stands on level ground and flies a kite. The string is taut and straight, 100 m long, and makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal ground. Take Aarav's hand to be at ground level.
(i) Find the height of the kite above the ground. [1]
(ii) Find the horizontal distance between Aarav and the point on the ground directly below the kite. [1]
(iii) The kite stays at the same height. Aarav walks towards the point below it until the string makes 45° with the ground. Find the new length of the string. (Use √2 = 1.41) [2]
OR
(iii) Find how far Aarav walked in the situation above. (Use √3 = 1.73) [2]

Apartment and the ground. A residential apartment block is 30 m high and stands on level ground. A point P on the ground, in line with the foot of the block, sees the top of the block at an angle of elevation of 60°.
(i) Find the distance of P from the foot of the block. [1]
(ii) What is the angle of depression of P as seen from the top of the block? Justify your answer. [1]
(iii) Rohan walks directly away from the block until the angle of elevation of the top becomes 30°. Find the distance he walked. (Use √3 = 1.73) [2]
OR
(iii) Find the length of the line of sight from Rohan to the top of the block when the angle of elevation is 30°. [2]

The painter's ladder. A painter uses a 16 m long ladder to reach a wall. The ladder rests against a vertical wall on level ground and makes an angle of 60° with the ground.
(i) How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall? [1]
(ii) How high up the wall does the ladder reach? (Leave in surd form.) [1]
(iii) For safety the painter changes the position of the foot of the ladder so that the same ladder makes 45° with the ground. Find how much lower the top of the ladder now is on the wall. (Use √2 = 1.41, √3 = 1.73) [2]
OR
(iii) Find how much farther from the wall the foot of the ladder now is. (Use √2 = 1.41) [2]

Balloon festival. A hot-air balloon hovers 90 m above level ground at a point directly above a spot O. Two observers A and B stand on opposite sides of O, in line with it. From A the angle of elevation of the balloon is 30° and from B it is 60°.
(i) Find the distance OA. [1]
(ii) Find the distance OB. [1]
(iii) Observer A walks towards O until the angle of elevation of the balloon is 45°. Find the distance A walked and the new distance between A and B (B has not moved). (Use √3 = 1.73) [2]
